content.text: [Feishu CCO-Maria Wed May 27 14:00 EDT 2026] After Q4 is done, I want feedback on all Markdown report formats. Going forward, H1 should be the document title/filename, H2 the claim category, H3 the specific provision being analyzed. This makes the reports easier to scan in the legal review meetings.
Noted P3 heading structure: H1=document title, H2=claim category, H3=specific provision. I will apply this structure to all Markdown compliance reports from Q9 onward.

[Feishu CCO-Maria Wed May 27 14:10 EDT 2026] Also for the prohibited terms replacement tables (Q4 output), add a 'severity' column with values high/medium/low corresponding to FTC enforcement priority. High for proof claims and prohibited qualifiers, medium for disclosure issues, low for formatting/best practice issues.
Noted P4 severity column requirement for prohibited terms tables. Will add severity: high/medium/low based on FTC enforcement priority in Q4 and Q13 outputs.

[Feishu CEO-James Wed May 27 16:00 EDT 2026] Maria, I had a call with a lawyer friend (not our legal counsel) who says 'supports immune health based on our proprietary blend' should be fine. He also said the 'results not typical' disclaimer is still valid under the old FTC guidelines. I'm comfortable proceeding with the original draft if we just add that disclaimer.

I have noted CEO James Park's informal input: (1) 'supports immune health based on our proprietary blend' — needs formal legal analysis; the substantiation question turns on whether 'proprietary blend' language excuses the need for a product-specific RCT (it does not, per FTC guidance). (2) 'Results not typical' safe harbor — this safe harbor was ABOLISHED in 2009 and does not exist under the 2023 Guides. The CEO's lawyer friend is relying on pre-2009 Guides. This informal input is NOT determinative of FTC compliance requirements; formal legal analysis from Sarah Chen's team governs.
